questions.question: Which of the following best describes the historiographical challenge identified by researchers around 2020 regarding post-classical history?
options: A global history of the period between 500 and 1500 is still wanting
World history research has focused too heavily on Afro-Eurasia
Medieval studies in Europe focused on individual nation-states
The Islamic World lacks a rich regional historiography
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that researchers around the year 2020 emphasized that "a global history of the period between 500 and 1500 is still wanting."
Incorrect. While the article notes that World History research has tended to focus on Afro-Eurasia, this is not the specific challenge identified by researchers around 2020.
Incorrect. The article mentions that medieval studies in Europe tended to focus on individual nation-states in the 19th century, but this is not the challenge identified around 2020.
Incorrect. The article states that the Islamic World has a rich regional historiography, so this option contradicts the text.

questions.question: According to the article, what is a key limitation of applying the term "post-classical" on a global scale?
options: It may be Eurocentric
It is synonymous with late antiquity
It corresponds only to Western European history
It excludes the Islamic Golden Age
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "the application of the term post-classical on a global scale is also problematic, and it may likewise be Eurocentric."

Incorrect. The article notes that academic publications sometimes use post-classical and late antiquity synonymously for Western Eurasia, but this is not identified as a limitation of global application.
Incorrect. The article explains that post-classical is used in world history beyond just Western Europe.
Incorrect. The article discusses the Islamic Golden Age as part of the post-classical period, so the term does not exclude it.

questions.question: Based on the article's discussion of world history periodization, which of the following is NOT one of the five or six major periods used by world historians?
options: Late antiquity
Early civilization
Classical societies
Post-classical
answer_explanations: Correct. The article lists early civilization, classical societies, post-classical, early modern, long nineteenth century, and contemporary/modern era as the major periods; late antiquity is not included in this list.
Incorrect. Early civilization is listed as the first major period in the article's enumeration.
Incorrect. Classical societies is listed as the second major period in the article's enumeration.
Incorrect. Post-classical is listed as the third major period in the article's enumeration.

questions.question: According to the article, which of the following best characterizes the political trends of the post-classical period?
options: There were no common global political trends
Feudalism was applied universally across all regions
Imperial China established a single political system for all of Asia
The Islamic empires created a unified political structure across Afro-Eurasia
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "there were no common global political trends during the post-classical period; rather, it was a period of loosely organized states and other developments, but no common political patterns emerged."
Incorrect. The article describes feudalism as applied in Western Europe, not universally across all regions.
Incorrect. The article notes China's dynastic cycle and influence on Japan, Korea, and Vietnam, but not a single political system for all of Asia.
Incorrect. The article describes the creation of Islamic empires as a new power in specific regions, not a unified political structure across Afro-Eurasia.

questions.question: According to the article, what was a consequence of the fall of Roman civilization in the Mediterranean and Europe?
options: It left a power vacuum and forced certain areas to build new civilizations entirely
It led to the immediate rise of the Islamic caliphates
It caused the complete disappearance of trade networks in Europe
It resulted in the universal adoption of feudalism across Europe
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "The fall of Roman civilization not only left a power vacuum for the Mediterranean and Europe, but forced certain areas to build what some historians might call new civilizations entirely."
Incorrect. The article discusses the spread of Islam and caliphates separately, not as an immediate consequence of Rome's fall.
Incorrect. The article describes expanding trade networks during the post-classical period, not their disappearance.
Incorrect. The article notes feudalism was applied in Western Europe, while Byzantium retained Roman features, so it was not universal.

questions.question: Based on the article, which of the following best describes the state of historical understanding of sub-Saharan Africa and the Americas during the post-classical period?
options: Understanding is far more limited compared to other regions
Well-established histories exist for these regions
These regions had extensive written records from the period
Trade networks connected these regions directly to Afro-Eurasia
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "Understanding of communication within sub-Saharan Africa or the Americas is, by contrast, far more limited."
Incorrect. The article says well-established histories exist for many regions, but contrasts this with the limited understanding of sub-Saharan Africa and the Americas.
Incorrect. The article does not mention extensive written records for these regions; instead it emphasizes limited understanding.
Incorrect. The article states the Americas had little contact with Afro-Eurasia before the Columbian exchange and their trade zones remained separate.

questions.question: According to the article, which of the following best describes the role of the Mongol Empire in post-classical trade and communication?
options: It established safe trade that allowed goods, cultures, ideas, and disease to spread between Asia, Europe, and Africa
It restricted trade between East and West
It focused exclusively on land-based conquest without encouraging exchange
It replaced the Silk Road with maritime routes only
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "the growth of the Mongol Empire in Central Asia established safe trade, which allowed goods, cultures, ideas, and disease to spread between Asia, Europe, and Africa."
Incorrect. The article describes the Mongol Empire as permitting more trade and cultural exchange, not restricting it.
Incorrect. The article emphasizes that the Mongol Empire facilitated exchange between regions, not conquest without exchange.
Incorrect. The article mentions the Silk Road continued to spread cultures and ideas, and does not say the Mongols replaced it with maritime routes only.

questions.question: Based on the article, which of the following best describes the spread of Buddhism during the post-classical period?
options: It spread from India into China and then to Japan, Korea, and Vietnam
It remained confined to India throughout the period
It spread primarily through European missionary efforts
It replaced Christianity as the dominant religion in Europe
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "Buddhism spread from India into China and flourished there briefly before using it as a hub to spread to Japan, Korea, and Vietnam."
Incorrect. The article explicitly describes Buddhism spreading beyond India to China, Japan, Korea, and Vietnam.
Incorrect. The article attributes the spread of Buddhism to regional diffusion from India via China, not European missionary efforts.
Incorrect. The article states Christianity became entrenched in Europe, not that Buddhism replaced it.

questions.question: According to the article, which of the following best describes the relationship between the post-classical period and the traditional tripartite periodization of Western European history?
options: Post-classical is not necessarily a member of the classical-middle-modern tripartite periodization
Post-classical is identical to the Middle Ages in all respects
Post-classical replaces the classical period in Western European history
Post-classical applies only to non-European regions
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "Although post-classical is synonymous with the Middle Ages of Western Europe, the term post-classical is not necessarily a member of the traditional tripartite periodization of Western European history into classical, middle, and modern."
Incorrect. While synonymous with the Middle Ages of Western Europe, the article clarifies it is not necessarily part of the tripartite periodization.
Incorrect. The article does not say post-classical replaces the classical period.
Incorrect. The article discusses post-classical as applicable globally, including Western Europe.

questions.question: Based on the article, which of the following best describes the assessment by Belich, Darwin, Frenz, and Wickham regarding global history?
options: Global history cannot usefully mean the history of everything, everywhere, all the time
Global history should focus exclusively on Afro-Eurasia
Global history is best defined as encompassing the whole planet at all times
Global history should ignore connectedness and transnational relationships
answer_explanations: Correct. The article quotes their assessment: "Global history may be boundless, but global historians are not. Global history cannot usefully mean the history of everything, everywhere, all the time."
Incorrect. The article discusses the need to move beyond exclusive focus on Afro-Eurasia, not to limit global history to it.
Incorrect. The article explicitly rejects defining globalization as always encompassing the whole planet.
Incorrect. The article lists connectedness, including transnational relationships, as one of three promising approaches.
